question: A man started working in a factory where he regularly had to work with steam and boiling water. On the first day, his doctor warned him to be more careful with steam because steam burns can be more serious than those from hot water. What is the reason for this?

options.text: Steam has more latent heat of vaporization
Steam may stick to the body

solution:
The correct answer is __**Steam has more latent heat of vaporization**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Steam has more latent heat of vaporization** compared to boiling water.
 
• When steam comes into contact with the skin, it releases this additional latent heat as it condenses into water, causing more severe burns.
